newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian bond yield falls ahead of extra sale.
newsitem.headline: Russian bond yield falls ahead of extra sale.

text.p: Low demand at an auction of Russian 728-day OFZ interest-bearing bonds ahead of an extra trading session pushed the yield above the current secondary market level as investors bid aggressively for the paper, dealers said on Wednesday.
But an auction of 364-day GKO discount Treasury bills attracted strong demand, pushing the average yield to the current secondary market levels, they said.

Demand for the 10.0 trillion roubles of bonds on offer was only four trillion roubles, and the average yield was 24.44 percent. On Tuesday another issue of two-year bonds closed at a yield of 23.22 percent.

After the auction the Finance Ministry, which is repaying earlier tax-exempt issues early, held a special trading session for the new bonds, where banks could only buy it from the government at the average price set at the auction.
"Banks demonstrated a low demand and forced the Finance Ministry to provide a premium on the bond and sell it at an average price after the auction," Rinaco-Plus dealer Alexander Gridin said.

Dealers forecast prices of outstanding bonds would fall tomorrow to today's auction levels, but prices of T-bills -- more attractive to foreign investors as they have a shorter maturity and pay a predictable effective interest rate -- would rise further as new funds flow in from the foreign exchange and equity markets.
